book.mystcraft.guide.page.1:
The Agewriter's Guide

An Age is a world described in a book. Gather pages, arrange their symbols, then explore what you have written.

Always bring a way home.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.2:
Getting started

You will need an Ink Mixer, a Book Binder, a Writing Desk, paper, ink and leather. A Collation Folder helps arrange pages.

Recipes begin on page 31.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.3:
Ink and panels

Make an Ink Vial with two ink sacs or black dyes and a water bottle. Put ink and paper in the Ink Mixer; take a Link Panel Page from the output.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.4:
A way home

Craft a Link Panel with leather to make an Unlinked Link Book. Use it at your home location to bind it there. Carry it before entering an Age.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.5:
Travel

At home, put the Descriptive Book on a Bookstand. Right-click it and click its panel. To return, use your home book and click its panel. Held books are left behind.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.6:
Finding pages

Visit village Archivists and explore libraries in the Overworld and Ages for symbol pages. Exploratory Ages can be unpredictable. Take a return book.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.7:
Copying pages

Put a folder in the Writing Desk target slot and owned pages or collections in a library tab. Supply paper and ink, then right-click a source page to copy it.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.8:
Copying pages

Each folder copy costs one paper and 50 mB of ink. Your source stays. ALL can show unowned pages in gray; these are a catalog, not free copies.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.9:
Arranging pages

Use a Collation Folder to store pages in order. In stored-order view, Alt-drag pages to rearrange them. Alphabetical view sorts the display, not the contents.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.10:
Binding an Age

Put leather in the Binder and enter a title. Insert one Link Panel first, then your pages. It must be the only panel. See page 36 for controls. Take the book.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.11:
Writing grammar

A modifier comes before the symbol it describes. Place biome pages before their distribution, and ground and sea materials before the world type.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.12:
Writing grammar

Choose one biome distribution, world type, weather and lighting. Extra controllers can add instability. Unspecified details may be filled in randomly.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.13:
Worked example

Write these in order, beginning with the Link Panel:

1. Link Panel Page
2. Plains
3. Single Biome Distribution
book.mystcraft.guide.page.14:
Worked example

Continue after Single Biome Distribution:

4. Mod Mat stone 0
5. No Seas
6. Standard World

The stone page is the ground material.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.15:
Worked example

Continue in order:

7. No Weather
8. Normal Lighting
9. Normal Sun
10. Normal Moon
11. Normal Stars
book.mystcraft.guide.page.16:
Reading the example

Plains feeds the single-biome controller. Stone and No Seas feed Standard World. The following pages set weather, lighting and celestial bodies.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.17:
Reading the example

This is a starting point, not a stability promise. Unwritten details, including celestial modifiers and features, can be chosen for you. No Seas does not forbid lakes.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.18:
Trying variations

Make a new book to compare one change at a time. Replace Plains with another biome page, or No Seas with Mod Mat water 0 for a water sea.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.19:
Biome choices

Single Biome takes one biome page; Native takes none. Tiled and Grid-form take at least two; Tiny through Huge take at least three. Put biomes first.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.20:
More modifiers

Colors, directions and lengths modify compatible symbols that follow. Keep each modifier beside its target. Unused modifiers can add instability. See page 37.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.21:
Clear Modifiers

A Clear Modifiers page clears unused pending modifiers. It still charges some instability for what it clears; it does not erase extra controllers or repair an Age.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.22:
Instability

Conflicting controllers, unused modifiers and valuable features or resources can add risk. Symptoms range from hunger to lightning and spreading decay.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.23:
Resource costs

Dense Ores, Bright Lighting and valuable material features can raise risk. Instability also uses a resource profile, so a quiet arrival is not proof of safety.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.24:
Watch and wait

Resource scoring needs a baseline and over 400 sampled Age chunks. It can change as more chunks are sampled. Explore cautiously before building a permanent base.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.25:
Reading the score

Operators can use /mystcraft instability inside an Age to see its score, sampled chunks and symbol cost. A zero score before profiling completes is not a guarantee.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.26:
Dangerous tradeoffs

Some written hazards reduce symbol cost, but still occur: Lightning, Meteors, Scorched Surface and Spontaneous Explosions are dangerous.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.27:
If things go wrong

Leave with your home book. Keep notes on your pages and symptoms. Check for duplicate controllers, unused modifiers and valuable resource features.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.28:
Try again

Once first linked, the Age's plan is fixed. Make a new book with corrected pages; change one thing at a time. The old Age does not become safe by editing a copy.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.29:
Before you link

Bind a home book. Check your page order and title. Leave valuables at home; pack food, blocks and spare return books. Keep the Descriptive Book somewhere safe.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.30:
Field notes

Observe the terrain, sky and effects. Record the pages and your changes. Modpacks can alter symbols and rules, so test each new design before settling in.

book.mystcraft.guide.page.36:
Binder controls

Hold a page or filled folder and click the numbered strip or + to insert. Click a page with an empty cursor to remove it; arrows scroll the strip.
book.mystcraft.guide.page.37:
Sun example

Replace Normal Sun with:

Mod Full
Mod East
Mod Rising
Normal Sun

Length, direction, then phase.
